prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit, realistic mechanical concept illustration.
EDIT TARGET: the provided image "A - PLATEAU OUVERT". Preserve this exact DIY robot chassis concept, its open aluminium plate silhouette, four black road wheels, two rear independent red cylindrical brushless motors with their two-stage spur-gear reductions, front passive steering with servo and tie rods, central low battery with straps, Pi5 electronics bridge, cooling heatsink, fuse holders, distribution blocks, manual red cutoff and wiring organisation. Retain the clean studio background and realistic CAD-style materials. This is an iteration of A, not a new chassis architecture.

MAIN CHANGE: move the ONE existing camera off the front bumper and install it HIGH at the REAR CENTRE on a small rigid removable two-post aluminium camera gantry. The front is the near foreground side with the two steering wheels; the rear is the far upper side with the two red motors. Camera must be at the FAR REAR, behind/above the Pi5 bridge, looking FORWARD over the chassis toward the front bumper and road ahead, with a modest downward tilt. The camera is an approximately32x32mm USB board-camera with a small black threaded lens, not a GoPro or a giant CCTV camera. Show its lens facing forward, toward the foreground, so the viewing direction is visually unambiguous. There must be exactly ONE camera, ONLY on this elevated rear gantry. Completely REMOVE the old low front camera and its bracket; leave a simple clean protected front bumper and the original steering mechanism. Do not leave a second lens at the front.

Gantry design: two slim rigid uprights bolted to the rear plate outside the motor gearing and clear of wheels, with modest gussets, joined by a slender crossbar. Central camera mount has visible side pivot screws and arcuate adjustment slots for adjustable tilt. Use a practical moderate height of roughly2 to3 tire diameters above the main deck; it must clear the electronics and see forward over them without a huge tower. Convey a removable bolted mount and cable strain relief. Route a SINGLE thin black USB cable from the camera down an upright, held by several small clips, then to a host USB port of the Pi. Do not show a white CSI ribbon: our selected camera is USB. Keep battery access, motor clearance, cooling and accessible power cutoff.

SECOND SMALL CORRECTION: remove the black external stick antenna near the Pi; Pi5 uses built-in WiFi and no extra antenna has been selected. Preserve all other hardware placement and wheel count. Do not redesign the motors, transmission or power architecture.

Composition: same elevated front-left three-quarter view as the input, slightly widen framing/leave extra headroom so the complete rear gantry is visible with all four wheels fully in frame. One main product view only, no inset, no collage. The raised rear-facing-to-front camera and its support are the clear focus of the revision, but the whole open platform remains readable. No field-of-view cone, no simulated FPV image and no claim that all the platform is guaranteed visible with this lens.
Text at top verbatim: "A2 - PLATEAU OUVERT, CAMÉRA ARRIÈRE"
Small footer verbatim: "Concept visuel - hauteur et cadrage à valider"
French typography, no other labels, no dimension lines, no extra sensors, extra cameras, extra wheels, propellers or futuristic styling.
